title: Correct acceleration value
description: Essential Criteria: The final numerical answer for part (1) must be 3 m/s².

title: Correct displacement value
description: Essential Criteria: The final numerical answer for part (2) must be 800 m.

title: Power-force-velocity relationship
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly apply the formula P = Fv to find the traction force at a given speed.

title: Newton's second law application
description: Important Criteria: The student must set up and solve Newton's second law (F_net = ma) using the traction and resistance forces.

title: Maximum speed condition
description: Important Criteria: The student must recognize that maximum speed is reached when traction force equals the constant resistance force.

title: Work-energy theorem application
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly apply the work-energy theorem (or integrate power) to relate work done, energy lost to friction, and the gain in kinetic energy.

title: Resistance force calculation
description: Optional Criteria: The student should explicitly calculate the constant resistance force as 0.1mg = 2000 N.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional Criteria: The student's solution should demonstrate consistent use of SI units (kW to W, etc.).

title: Sign error in net force
description: Pitfall Criteria: Deduct points if the student incorrectly sets the net force as (F_f - F) or misplaces the sign in Newton's second law.

title: Incorrect power conversion
description: Pitfall Criteria: Deduct points if the student fails to convert the rated power from kW to W (80 kW to 80000 W).
